# `silk/compress/lzma2`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Decode complete raw LZMA2 streams into caller-owned byte buffers.

## When to use
Use [`Lzma2.decode`](#Lzma2.impl.decode) when a surrounding protocol supplies the dictionary size. For `.xz` files,
use `silk.compress.xz.Xz`, which reads the dictionary size and verifies the container.

## Details
Supports stored and range-coded chunks, dictionary resets, property changes, and state reuse.
Input must contain exactly one stream including its zero end byte. Raw LZMA2 has no checksum.
The output buffer holds dictionary history. Probability tables use the ambient allocator.

Import as `Lzma2` with `import silk.compress.lzma2 { Lzma2 }`.

### Associated function `decode`

```silk
pub effect fn decode(
    input: &[u8],
    output: &mut [u8],
    dictionaryBytes: u64,
    limits: DecodeLimits
  ) -> Decoded
    ! OutOfMemoryError | DecodeError
    ? &mut Allocator
```

Decodes one raw LZMA2 stream into the start of `output`, with the supplied dictionary size.

#### Details
`dictionaryBytes` must be between 4096 and 4294967295. The output buffer holds history;
only probability tables allocate. Stored and compressed chunks, all reset modes, and property
changes are supported. The zero end byte is mandatory, and trailing bytes are rejected.
Raw LZMA2 has no checksum. Returns the consumed and written lengths.

#### Errors
`DecodeError` reports invalid properties, chunk sequences, ranges, distances, sizes, truncated
or trailing input, and resource limits. Discard output on failure. `OutOfMemoryError` reports
failure to allocate probability tables through the ambient allocator.
